verdict.headline: US strikes on Iran push oil to a six-week high and finally crack the stock market
verdict.label: Brent settled $94.65 (+4.6%) and WTI $90.22 (+5.2%) after CENTCOM struck IRGC sites at noon ET. The S&P 500 lost 7,650 to close at 7,631.47 (-0.71%), Nasdaq -1.03%, Russell 2000 -1.23%. ISM Manufacturing 54.6 with the Prices Index unchanged at 71.1; JOLTS 7.271M with June revised down 177,000; September hike odds 68%; 10Y 4.79%, 30Y 5.28%; gold -1.86%.
verdict.rationale_short: Oil is transmitting to equities through the discount rate rather than the earnings line: ISM showed demand cooling to 53.7 new orders while input prices held at 71.1, so a supply shock now argues for tighter policy instead of easier. Equities absorbed nine sessions of that repricing without flinching and then took it in one afternoon, led from the long-duration end. A Brent close back under $90 or a 30-year close under 5.15% dissolves the frame; Brent above $100 with the 30-year settling above 5.30% extends it.

supporting_data.label: CENTCOM began striking IRGC air defence, radar, naval and mine-laying sites in southern Iran at noon ET, after two supertankers were hit near the Strait of Hormuz
Brent settled $4.16 higher at $94.65 (+4.6%), highest since July 24; WTI settled up $4.46 at $90.22 (+5.2%), highest since July 23
September hike odds reached 68% on CME FedWatch, up from roughly 36% before Jackson Hole
ISM Manufacturing 54.6 versus 55.6 in July; Prices Index unchanged at 71.1 while New Orders fell three points to 53.7
JOLTS openings 7.271M in July, below the 7.33-7.36M consensus, with June revised down 177,000 to 7.182M
Anthropic signed a six-year, $35B cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda in which Nvidia holds the lease on the Texas data centre

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 2.36% to $459.61 with the semis, on discount-rate pressure rather than company news; a 30-year close back under 5.25% is what unwinds the group's derating.

Down roughly 1% as Anthropic's $35B six-year deal with Lambda left Nvidia as chip supplier, equity holder in both counterparties and lessee of the Texas data centre. The question raised is financing circularity, not demand.
Fell below $77,000 to about $76,762 on the strikes, with roughly $115M of long liquidations inside an hour. The $76,661 support is now at the price rather than below it.
Gold fell 1.86% to $4,358.74, a third consecutive decline into an escalating conflict — the clearest sign the tape is pricing inflation rather than fear.
WTI settled at $90.22, up 5.2% and its first close above $90 since July 23.

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has traded above 5.30% in two separate sessions and closed there in neither, settling at 5.28% today. Treasury long-dated buyback operations beginning September 9 are the offsetting structural bid against the oil-inflation input.
trade_setups.entry: A daily close above 5.30% marks the level crossed rather than tagged; a close back under 5.15% says the buyback bid is absorbing supply at the long end
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent back under $90 or a payrolls print under 150K removes the inflation impulse driving the move
trade_setups.horizon: This week, with the September 4 jobs report the decisive test

trade_setups.thesis: Two supertankers have been hit and US forces have struck the mine-laying capability behind it, yet crude is still transiting Hormuz. The distinction that matters is between headline escalation and measured supply disruption, and transit behaviour marks it, not strike counts.
trade_setups.entry: Voluntary transit suspensions by major operators put $100 in play; a return under $90 says the premium is decaying on July's schedule
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed halt in hostilities or Gulf mediation collapses the premium built over three sessions

trade_setups.thesis: The index lost 7,650 in one afternoon after absorbing nine sessions of the same rate move, and the adjustment came from the long-duration end — Nasdaq -1.03% and Russell -1.23% against the Dow's -0.79%. The VIX ended above 16 after closing under 15 on August 31, so an event premium now exists where there was none.
trade_setups.entry: Holding 7,580 through Thursday says one afternoon completed the adjustment; losing 7,550 says multiples are still repricing into payrolls
trade_setups.invalidation: A reclaim of 7,700 on softer oil returns the tape to its pre-strike range

bear_case: The read treats a war-risk premium as an inflation regime. Brent at $94.65 is only its highest since July 24 and WTI at $90.22 its highest since July 23 — a retest of summer levels, not a breakout, and every escalation premium this year has decayed within days of the last strike. The growth evidence cuts against the read as well: ISM at 54.6 is the eighth consecutive month of expansion, and a labour market whose openings were revised down 177,000 will not sustain 68% hike odds through a soft payrolls print. If Brent closes back under $90 and the S&P reclaims 7,700, this read no longer holds.
